description: Registry of executable capabilities. Every entrypoint is a public function in uiux.api; adapters call tools only through uiux.api.call_tool or the unified CLI (python scripts/uiux_cli.py call <id>). When passing parameters via CLI on Windows, prefer --params "@path/to/params.json" to avoid shell quoting issues. `input` is the JSON Schema subset enforced by uiux.core.schema before every call. `output.required` lists the top-level keys every successful result contains. `annotations` are platform-neutral upper bounds over all argument values: read_only, writes_to (none|target-project), may_start_process, deterministic, network_access, filesystem_read (package|target-project|browser-cache), requires_node, requires_browser, long_running.

tools.description: DEFAULT for normal UI tasks. Advances exactly one SEE?KNOW?THINK?DO?CHECK phase per call and persists handoffs in the target project?s existing .evidence storage. Repeatedly call it using the returned task_id and next_action until status is COMPLETED, PARTIAL, BLOCKED, or FAILED. Use for end-to-end UI work; do not use it to invoke a single low-level diagnostic. Example: run_ui_task(request="Improve checkout UI on mobile while keeping the brand colors"). Common blocked state: P0 context is insufficient, P2 requires permission, P3 finds a deviation, or P4 runtime evidence is unavailable.

request.description: Required on the first call. Original UI request; omit on continuation.

user_message.description: Only supply when next_action requests missing input or explicit permission. Never fabricate permission.

verbosity.description: compact returns envelope and refs; standard adds key summaries; full includes current canonical phase artifacts.

output.description: Task envelope. CHECK adds execution_status, verification_status, trust_level, limitations, and next_action. COMPLETED requires required verification PASS or PASS_WITH_WARNINGS.
